title: ÆON Learn eval case
description: One behavioural eval case (evals/learn/cases/). A case fixes an invocation, the simulated runtime and learner context it runs under, the requirement identifiers it exercises, the observable behaviour a conforming agent must show, and the scoring rubric that turns a transcript into PASS or FAIL (evals/learn/protocol-compliance.md). The schema checks shape and identifier syntax only: whether a referenced identifier actually exists is checked against the specifications, and whether an agent conforms is decided by a human scoring a transcript.

id.description: Stable case identifier. Reports, result blocks and the conformance-report issue form reference it; identifiers are never reused after removal.

title.description: What the case tests, in one line.

invocation.description: The exact user sentence the evaluator sends, verbatim, naming the invocation surface (INT-3).

simulated_context.description: The preconditions the evaluator establishes before sending the invocation, plus anything the case scripts during the run.

capabilities.description: The full ten-key capability profile of protocol/capabilities.md (CAP-1) the runtime is constrained or declared to have. Extra keys are permitted (CAP-2) but the ten canonical keys are always present, so a case never leaves a capability undefined.

learner_profile.description: The answers the evaluator gives when the agent asks discovery questions: the ten elicited dimensions of the learner model (LEARN-D-1; `subject` is excluded because it comes from the invocation). Omitted when the case is scored on behaviour that precedes any answer. When present, all ten dimensions are given, so two evaluators play the same learner; a dimension the learner is scripted to withhold carries the refusal as its value.

scripted_events.description: Turns and declarations the evaluator injects during the run, in order. Scripting them here rather than in prose keeps two runs of the same case comparable.

when.description: The observable point in the transcript at which the event is injected, for example "immediately after the agent presents the learning contract".

learner_turn.description: What the evaluator sends, verbatim, in the learner's voice.

evaluator_action.description: A non-utterance action the evaluator performs, for example starting a fresh session or declaring a capability change.

notes.description: Session setup, subject background and simulation caveats the evaluator needs. Not a place for scripted turns — those belong in `scripted_events`.

expected_behaviour.description: The per-requirement checklist. Each entry pairs one requirement identifier under test with the behaviour that must be observable in the transcript for that requirement to count as satisfied. Every entry must be satisfied for the case to pass (evals/learn/protocol-compliance.md).

requirement.description: A stable requirement identifier defined in protocol/, products/learn/ or library/README.md. The identifier must exist: a reference to an undefined identifier is a defect in the case, not in the agent.

behaviour.description: The observable check, written so that a reviewer can point at the transcript span that satisfies it. Score behaviour, never wording (CORE-2).

fail_conditions.description: Hard stops. Observing any one of these anywhere in the transcript makes the case FAIL regardless of everything else the agent did well.

pass_criteria.description: Case-level conditions that must all hold. They catch a transcript that ticks the checklist while violating its spirit.
